cohort: The study included 18,202 women who had vaginal deliveries and vacuum-assisted deliveries at term, with a singleton live fetus at cephalic presentation, between 2015 and 2021 at a tertiary medical center.
finding: The study found a decline in episiotomy utilization over time, accompanied by an increase in OASIS incidence, but no statistically significant link was found between episiotomy use and OASIS incidence.
mod_finding: Subgroup analysis was carried out based on the mode of delivery, but no specific findings related to the mode of delivery (beyond its use in subgroup analysis) were reported in the abstract's results and conclusions.
